title: The same misdetection then FABRICATES values that were never in the input
rationale: Once one value promotes the parent to an array, every sibling is dragged in, and reconstructArray pads short fields by REPEATING their last element. A field that occurred once in the input appears three times in the output. That is not lossy - it is invention, with no marker, and a downstream consumer cannot tell the duplicates from real repetition.
catchesBugClass: Value fabrication during reconstruction. Padding-by-repetition is far more dangerous than the null-padding on the flatten side, because repeated real values look legitimate while padded nulls look like gaps.
cannotCatch: Cannot distinguish fabricated repetition from genuine repetition by inspecting the output alone. It also cannot tell whether the last-value padding is ever CORRECT.

predicted.detail: Only c triggers detection but arrayPaths is keyed on the shared prefix, so b is pulled in and its single 7 is replicated into three records.
